_about: William Warde Fowler (1847-1921), Oxford historian of Roman religion. Classical scholarship (lane B pivot of 2026-10-10 from translations to public-domain English scholarship on the classics): Social Life at Rome in the Age of Cicero, The Religious Experience of the Roman People, from the Earliest Times to the Age of Augustus, Rome (Home University Library), The Roman Festivals of the Period of the Republic, clean Gutenberg. His bird books are outside the brief. No uids minted. Also Julius Caesar and the Foundation of the Roman Imperial System (Putnam, 1892), raw IA OCR. Round dw (2026-10-23) added, raw IA OCR with title pages read: The City-State of the Greeks and Romans (1893); Virgil's Messianic Eclogue (1907, three studies with J. B. Mayor and R. S. Conway); Roman Ideas of Deity (1914); Virgil's Gathering of the Clans (1916); Aeneas at the Site of Rome (1918); The Death of Turnus (1919); Roman Essays and Interpretations (1920). Not taken: his books on birds (outside lane B's scope).
